title: Ethical Storytelling and Consent
disclaimer: Synthetic training document for an educational project. Not an official policy, report or donor record of any real organization.
content:
Stories and images are powerful fundraising tools, but they must protect the dignity, safety and rights of the people shown, especially children and families in crisis.

Ethical storytelling means presenting people as active participants in their own lives, not as helpless victims. Avoid images that are shocking or humiliating, and do not exaggerate needs to increase donations.

Always obtain informed consent before using a person's story, photo or video. Consent must be given freely, in a language the person understands, and they must know where the content will be published. For children, obtain consent from a parent or guardian and also seek the child's own agreement where appropriate.

Protect identities when there is any risk of harm. Change names, avoid showing exact locations, and never publish details that could identify a child who is a survivor of violence or exploitation.

Stories should be accurate and verified. Fundraising content must not invent quotes, combine different people into one story without disclosure, or claim results that the programme did not achieve.

Keep a record of consent for each story and respect requests to withdraw content.
